meta.title: Prelude in E Minor (Op. 28, No. 4 - Opening 12 Bars)

theory.summary: Chopin's masterclass in chromatic voice-leading: a singing tied melody floating above slowly descending left-hand triads.
theory.pattern_tip: Watch the left-hand chords slide downward one half-step at a time (G -> F# -> F -> E -> Eb -> D -> C -> B).
theory.technique_tip: Play the repeated left-hand 8th chords legato with forearm weight while sustaining the sighing right-hand half-step.
theory.ballade_link: Directly trains the chromatic inner-voice voice-leading and sorrowful rubato cantabile of Chopin's ballads.
concept_paragraphs: Chopin's E-minor Prelude looks intimidating on a Roman-numeral sheet (V4/2/iv, ii6/5/V, viio7/V), yet at the piano it follows one crystal-clear secret: the Left Hand slides down a chromatic staircase almost one note at a time!
Each repeated 8th-note triad changes just ONE voice by half-step while the Right Hand floats a tied, sighing melody overhead. Learn to spot which single finger steps downward from bar to bar.

form_map.role: Opening pickup sigh over Em/G descending chromatically past F#m7b5 and Dm7/F to Am/E.
Chromatic slide continues through Adim7/Eb and E7/D into Am/C -> B7.
Settles onto Em/B (i6/4) and poignant B7 dominant pause expecting resolution.

practice_steps: 1. Click the Roman numerals above the staff in Practice tab anytime to inspect any single chromatic chord.
2. Practice LH alone in Skeleton/Wait mode, watching one inner voice melt down a half-step per change.
3. Hold the tied RH melody tones serenely while pulsing the soft LH accompaniment underneath.
4. Perform quietly at 60 BPM without rushing the sighing half-step drops.
